category_name: Где ты бы встретил Новый год
current_p1_ru: Бали, Мальдивы, Бангкок, Дубай. Тебе нужен Новый год без зимы. В то время как все мерзнут — ты на пляже, с коктейлем, в шортах.
current_p1_en:
Bali, the Maldives, Bangkok, Dubai. You need New Year's without winter. While everyone freezes, you're on the beach, cocktail in hand, in shorts.
Your relationship with tradition is healthy. No one said New Year's has to be winter. You break the mold.
People sometimes don't get it: "what tree on the beach?" None. That's the point: a holiday without mandatory props.
What's worth knowing: tropics on New Year's is also escapism. Sometimes people leave to avoid being with close ones, and then feel sad. Learn to tell "I'm choosing warmth" from "I'm running from something". The first — great. The second — needs a different solution.

category_name: Где ты бы встретил Новый год
current_p1_ru: Горнолыжный курорт, Рейкьявик с северным сиянием, Эдинбург с Hogmanay, горы у костра. Тебе нужен Новый год с настоящей зимой — снег, холод, северные традиции.
current_p1_en:
A ski resort, Reykjavík under northern lights, Edinburgh for Hogmanay, mountains by a fire. You need New Year's with real winter: snow, cold, northern ritual.
You have a romance with the north. The standard olivier-at-home scene bores you; you need atmosphere, weather, nature.
People sometimes say: "but it's expensive." Expensive, yes. But the northern lights don't compare to anything else.
What's worth knowing: northern destinations require preparation. Cold, weather, sometimes flight delays. Plan ahead. A spontaneous Reykjavik trip in December can end badly.

category_name: Где ты бы встретил Новый год
current_p1_ru: Прага, Барселона, Амстердам, Эдинбург. Ты любишь Новый год в красивых европейских городах. Не «событие века», а просто прекрасный фон для маленького праздника.
current_p1_en:
Prague, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Edinburgh. You like New Year's in beautiful European cities. Not "the event of the century", just a beautiful backdrop for a small celebration.
You have a sense of measure. You don't need to fly to Sydney; a beautiful European capital for the weekend is enough.
People sometimes ask: "how many times can you go to Prague?" Endlessly. Each time is different.
What's worth knowing: European classics also mean overcrowded hotels at New Year's. Prices triple. Plan ahead. Booking in August for December is normal.

category_name: Где ты бы встретил Новый год
current_p1_ru: Токио в тишине, Стамбул на двух континентах, Бангкок с храмами, Дубай. Тебе ближе восточный Новый год — другая эстетика, другие традиции, другой темп.
current_p1_en:
Tokyo in silence, Istanbul on two continents, Bangkok with temples, Dubai. The Eastern New Year's is closer to you — different aesthetics, different traditions, different tempo.
You're curious about other cultures. Western New Year's traditions are familiar; you want to widen the frame.
People sometimes don't get it: "Tokyo doesn't celebrate New Year like we do." Exactly. It has its own way, and that's what makes it interesting.
What's worth knowing: Eastern New Year's is a different culture. If you expect from Tokyo a noisy Times Square party — you'll be disappointed. Learn to accept local traditions, not to fit them to your template.

category_name: Где ты бы встретил Новый год
current_p1_ru: Северное сияние в Рейкьявике, два континента в Стамбуле, тишина Токио, дом с близкими. Тебе важно, чтобы Новый год был не «как у всех», а с уникальным переживанием.
current_p1_en:
Northern lights in Reykjavik, two continents in Istanbul, the silence of Tokyo, home with close ones. What matters is that New Year's isn't "like everyone's" but with a unique experience.
You collect special moments. Not for Instagram — for your own memory. In 30 years, these are the New Year's nights you'll still remember.
People sometimes don't get it: "you're flying so far for one night?" For one night you'll remember your whole life. Different category.
What's worth knowing: "special moments" sometimes don't happen. The lights didn't appear, the fireworks were canceled, the weather turned. Learn to accept it. The trip itself is the experience, even if the climax falls through.

current_p1_ru: Бокс, MMA, дзюдо, BJJ, теннис, баскетбол. Тебе нужен прямой контакт с противником. Не «один на один с природой» — а игра, в которой важно реакция, скорость, техника против другого человека.
current_p1_en:
Boxing, MMA, judo, BJJ, tennis, basketball. You need direct contact with an opponent. Not one-on-one with nature, but a live human on the other side: reaction, speed, technique.
You're competitive by nature. Training without a live opponent bores you; you need to measure yourself against someone.
People sometimes worry: "what about injuries?" They happen. You know what you're signing up for.
What's worth knowing: contact sports require discipline and a good coach. Without them — injuries. Don't cheap out on the trainer. And remember: recovery is half the success. Without it, you don't grow — you just break down.

current_p1_ru: Баскетбол, волейбол, танцы, теннис. Тебе нужны люди рядом. Не одиночное упражнение; а ритм с другими, синхронизация, общая цель.
current_p1_en:
Basketball, volleyball, dance, tennis. You need people next to you. Not solo exercise, but rhythm with others, synchronization, a shared goal.
You have social energy. Sport without people turns into a gym session for you, and that's boring.
People sometimes say: "you could go alone." You could. But you need the moment of being in it together — that's when you train longer and better.
What's worth knowing: team sports require a schedule and people. Without a regular group, you don't grow. Learn to invest in the team, not just in your own form.

current_p1_ru: Плавание, дайвинг, гребля, сёрфинг. Тебе нужна вода. Под водой звуки тишают, на воде ритм размеренный, в волне — связь с природой.
current_p1_en:
Swimming, diving, rowing, surfing. You need water. Underwater the sounds quiet down, on the water the rhythm is steady, in the wave — connection with nature.
You have a meditative side. Most sports are about tension; water is about relaxation through motion.
People sometimes ask: "how can you spend hours in the pool?" Hours. It's a different relationship with time.
What's worth knowing: water sports require consistency. Skip two weeks and your form drops faster than in the gym. Learn regularity. And take care of your ears, sinuses — typical problems for those who spend a lot of time in water.

current_p1_ru: Хайкинг, скалолазание, велоспорт, гребля. Тебе нужно быть на свежем воздухе и в красивых местах. Тренажёрный зал тебе скучен; нужен пейзаж как часть тренировки.
current_p1_en:
Hiking, climbing, cycling, rowing. You need fresh air and beautiful places. The gym bores you; you need landscape as part of the workout.
Your connection with nature runs deep. City life doesn't give you enough oxygen, so you take it back outdoors.
People sometimes don't get it: "why drag yourself uphill for five hours?" Because the top is what you live for.
What's worth knowing: nature doesn't forgive mistakes. Learn to pack right, check weather, have a plan B. The most beautiful routes can become dangerous when you're underprepared.

current_p1_ru: Йога, плавание, танцы, бег. Тебе важна не «победа», а связь с собственным телом. Через дыхание, через ритм, через движение в потоке.
current_p1_en:
Yoga, swimming, dance, running. What matters isn't victory, but connection with your own body: through breath, rhythm, movement in flow.
You're looking for integration. Most workouts split the head from the body; you want the place where they meet.
People sometimes say: "yoga isn't a sport." It is. One of the hardest, because there's nothing to defeat except yourself.
What's worth knowing: integral practices work on regularity, not intensity. An hour of yoga every day gives more than three hours once a week. Learn to prioritize daily practice over the perfect session.

current_p1_ru: Марафон, велоспорт, хайкинг, плавание на длинные. Тебе нужна выносливость, а не скорость. Час за часом, своим ритмом.
current_p1_en:
Marathon, cycling, hiking, long-distance swimming. You need endurance, not speed. Hour after hour, at your own pace.
You have patience. Sprinting bores you; you need the challenge to last.
People sometimes don't understand: "hours of the same motion?" Hours. And every hour is a different landscape inside you.
What's worth knowing: distance sports require slow building. If you suddenly start a marathon without prep, injuries are guaranteed. Learn gradualness. And remember — recovery matters more than it seems. Not every day a long workout.

current_p1_ru: Apple, Dyson, Bose, Nothing. Ты выбираешь не «характеристики», а «ощущение». Эти бренды продают не функции — они продают опыт. И ты готов(-а) платить за это.
current_p1_en:
Apple, Dyson, Bose, Nothing. You don't pick specs; you pick the feeling. These brands don't just sell features. They sell experience, and you're willing to pay for it.
Your relationship with tech is mature. The spec sheet isn't the whole truth. Build quality, the feel of materials, the sound of the box closing — it's all part of the product.
People sometimes don't get it: "why Apple when Samsung is cheaper and faster?" Because Apple isn't just a phone. It's an ecosystem, a habit, a culture — and you're comfortable in it.
What's worth knowing: premium aesthetics costs. Sometimes it's worth checking — are you paying for craft or just for the logo? With the best of these brands the answer is craft. With the worst — only the logo.

current_p1_ru: Samsung, OnePlus, Xiaomi, Huawei. Ты выбираешь Android-устройства. Не «дёшево вместо Apple», а сознательный выбор: открытость, кастомизация, спецификации, выбор.
current_p1_en:
Samsung, OnePlus, Xiaomi, Huawei. You choose Android. Not "cheap instead of Apple," but a conscious choice: openness, customization, specs, options.
You have a geek's sensibility. You like being able to change, configure, expand. Apple feels too closed for you.
People sometimes tease: "still on Android?" Yes. And there's more freedom here than they think.
What's worth knowing: Android is variety, but also fragmentation. Not all apps have the same quality; updates can be uneven. Learn to choose. Not every Android flagship holds the level of an iPhone — but the best ones do, and they're there if you look.

current_p1_ru: Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta. Тебе ближе компании-сервисы. Не «железо», а «облако». Они дают тебе экосистему через приложения, а не через гаджеты.
current_p1_en:
Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta. You're closer to service companies. Not hardware — cloud. They build ecosystems through apps, not gadgets.
You understand the future is in the cloud. Hardware becomes secondary; data and services matter, and these companies are strong there.
People sometimes say: "Apple is cooler." Apple is great at hardware. In services, it often trails Google.
What's worth knowing: living in cloud ecosystems is convenient, but a risk — your data is theirs, and you're their hostage. Learn to keep copies of important things; don't trust one provider fully. Cloud lock-in is a real cost.

current_p1_ru: Sony, Bose, DJI, GoPro. Ты выбираешь технику для конкретного: записывать, снимать, слушать. Не «универсал», а «специалист».
current_p1_en:
Sony, Bose, DJI, GoPro. You pick gear for a specific purpose: record, film, listen. Not all-rounders — specialists.
You have a specific passion: maybe photography, maybe video, maybe music. You don't want compromise; you want the best in the niche.
People sometimes don't get it: "why DJI when your iPhone shoots?" Your iPhone shoots. DJI flies. Different tools.
What's worth knowing: specialization needs serious investment. Of money and time. Without regular practice, an expensive GoPro will sit on the shelf. Be honest with yourself: are you really going to use it, or do you just like the idea?

current_p1_ru: Xiaomi, OnePlus, Huawei, Amazon. Ты понял, что флагман по цене флагмана — глупость. Можно получить 90% возможностей за 50% стоимости, и эти бренды это доказывают.
current_p1_en:
Xiaomi, OnePlus, Huawei, Amazon. You know buying a flagship at flagship prices can be silly. You can get 90% of the capability for 50% of the price, and these brands prove it.
You have a financial instinct. You don't fall for marketing; you look at specs and compare.
People sometimes get snobby: "you're not on Apple." You're not. So what? Your phone takes better photos than many iPhones and costs half as much.
What's worth knowing: budget brands save, but sometimes on materials or support. Learn to tell "cheap and smart" from "cheap and cheap". The first is a win. The second is a trap that you discover six months later.

current_p1_ru: Tesla, Nothing, Meta, DJI. Тебе нравятся бренды, которые делают то, чего не делал никто. Электромобили, прозрачные телефоны, VR-гарнитуры, дроны — всё это в твоём фокусе, потому что ты следишь за тем, как меняется мир.
current_p1_en:
Tesla, Nothing, Meta, DJI. You like brands trying what no one else has done. Electric cars, transparent phones, VR headsets, drones — all on your radar, because you watch the world changing.
You have a nose for tomorrow. Most people use what's already there; you try what just appeared.
People sometimes call you an early adopter. Yes. And yes, you sometimes get burned on raw products. That's the price.
What's worth knowing: early products are an experiment. If you don't want to be the brand's tester, don't buy the first generation of anything. Wait for v2 — usually most issues are fixed.

current_p1_ru: Streetwear, кроссы, оверсайз, athleisure, hypebeast — твоя территория. Ты понял, что комфорт и стиль не противоречат, и одеваешься так, чтобы и тело было свободно, и взгляд цеплялся.
current_p1_en:
Streetwear, sneakers, oversize, athleisure, hypebeast — your territory. You know comfort and style don't contradict, and you dress so the body is free and the eye has something to catch.
Your life has a moving rhythm. You don't just sit in an office for eight hours; you move, ride, meet. Clothes should match that: allow, not restrict, and still carry the look.
People sometimes call this unserious. Seriousness isn't in creased slacks. It's in how you do the work. Street style doesn't get in the way — often, it helps.
What's worth knowing: streetwear ages quickly. Limiteds and hypebeasts lose value in a year. Learn to separate the eternal base (good sneakers, quality hoodie) from fashion noise. Otherwise in two years half your wardrobe will be irrelevant.

current_p1_ru: Old money, quiet luxury, preppy, business casual без логотипов. Ты понял, что настоящая дороговизна — это не показ, а ткань. Кашемир, который никто не узнает, но который чувствуется. Покрой, который сидит идеально без громких ярлыков.
current_p1_en:
Old money, quiet luxury, preppy, business casual without logos. You know real expense isn't display; it's fabric. Cashmere nobody recognizes but everyone feels. A cut that sits perfectly without a loud label.
Your attitude toward status is mature. You don't need to prove anything with a brand on your chest. Those who can see will see, even without a logo.
People sometimes miss it: "so what, a gray coat." The coat is real cashmere and cost real money. Only those who know will recognize it. Perfect.
What's worth knowing: quiet luxury works with those who notice. With others you're just "a person in boring clothes". Learn to accept that not every effort will be read. Style is for those who understand it, not for everyone.

current_p1_ru: Dark academia, grunge, avant-garde — твоя территория. Чёрный, кожа, рваное, осенние оттенки, иногда непонятно «что это вообще». Ты не одеваешься «красиво» по конвенциональным меркам — ты одеваешься так, как чувствуешь.
current_p1_en:
Dark academia, grunge, avant-garde — your territory. Black, leather, torn edges, autumn shades, sometimes an honest "what even is this." You don't dress beautifully by conventional standards; you dress how you feel.
You have your own aesthetic, and it runs deeper than fashion. You don't follow trends; you live in a visual universe that stays with you for years.
People sometimes ask: "why so gloomy?" It isn't gloomy. It's serious. Dark tones carry a gravity light ones can't.
What's worth knowing: dark aesthetics are beautiful, but require precision. Black should be perfectly black, not faded. Leather — real. Torn — thought-out. Otherwise you don't look conceptual, you look unkempt. The standard is high, and it must be held.

current_p1_ru: Cottage core, boho, vintage thrift — твоя ниша. Лён, цветы, слои, секонд-хенд с историей. Ты не «модно одеваешься» — ты создаёшь вокруг себя визуальный мир, в котором тебе спокойно.
current_p1_en:
Cottagecore, boho, vintage thrift — your niche. Linen, flowers, layers, secondhand with a story. You don't dress fashionably so much as build a visual world where you feel calm.
Your connection with nature and the past is strong. Modern clothing often feels sterile and disposable. You need a story, a fabric, or a craft behind every item.
People sometimes call this unmodern. You smile. Modernity is exactly this split: either synthetic mass market, or something living and chosen.
What's worth knowing: this aesthetic is beautiful, but not always practical. Linen wrinkles, vintage requires care, layers are harder in heat. Learn to alternate — sometimes more practical days. Otherwise your style becomes tiring even for yourself.

current_p1_ru: Минимализм, скандинавский, чёрно-белый. У тебя в комнате нет лишнего. Каждая вещь имеет функцию или смысл; всё, что не имеет — ушло. Ты одеваешь свою комнату как одеваешь себя — без излишеств.
current_p1_en:
Minimalism, Scandinavian, black-and-white. There's nothing extra in your room. Every object has a function or meaning; everything else is gone. You dress your room the way you dress yourself — without excess.
You have a clear head, and you need a clear environment around it. Chaos in the room means chaos in the head, and you don't want that.
People sometimes call your room cold: "like a hospital." Not a hospital — a gallery. A gallery also has few objects, but that doesn't make it cold. It makes it focused.
What's worth knowing: minimalism requires discipline. If you don't watch, in a year you'll find your "empty room" has accumulated things, and the aesthetic is destroyed. Regularly do an audit: what's gone from function? Without this work, minimalism slowly turns into ordinary disorder with white walls.

current_p1_ru: Hygge, ботанический, «просто дом». Свечи, пледы, растения, тёплый свет. Твоя комната — это место, куда ты приходишь восстанавливаться. И каждый элемент в ней об этом помнит.
current_p1_en:
Hygge, botanical, "just home." Candles, blankets, plants, warm light. Your room is where you come to recover, and every element remembers that.
You understand that home isn't where you sleep; it's where you live. It should hold what you need for life — not what impresses guests.
People sometimes marvel at the number of candles: "how many can there be?" As many as you want. The criterion isn't "what's accepted"; it's "what I need."
What's worth knowing: coziness is an aesthetic that can become a trap. If your room is too warm and pleasant, you stop leaving. Learn to make home a recovery, not a refuge. The line between these two states is thin, and it's important to track it.

current_p1_ru: Dark academia, vintage, индустриальный лофт. Дерево, кожа, книги, тёмные тона, потолочные балки. Твоя комната — это место, в котором хочется писать роман.
current_p1_en:
Dark academia, vintage, industrial loft. Wood, leather, books, dark tones, ceiling beams. Your room makes you want to write a novel.
Your connection with the past and with intellect runs deep. You're not just a modern person in a modern apartment; you live in a space that points to centuries, thought, craft.
People sometimes ask: "do you live in a library?" Almost. And it suits you very well.
What's worth knowing: dark academia requires care for details. If books on the shelf are for beauty, not for reading — that's posing, not style. If a leather chair is cracked not from long use but from poor quality — that also shows. This aesthetic works only with authentic things.

current_p1_ru: Wabi-sabi, минимализм, ботанический. Пустота, природа, имперфектная красота. Ты понял японскую идею — что в недосказанности есть глубина, в нескольких предметах больше смысла, чем в полной комнате.
current_p1_en:
Wabi-sabi, minimalism, botanical. Emptiness, nature, imperfect beauty. You understand the Japanese idea: understatement has depth, and a few objects can mean more than a full room.
Your relationship with space is meditative. A room isn't a container for things; it's an organism with its own rules.
People sometimes call it empty: "you have nothing." Not nothing — nothing extra. Different category.
What's worth knowing: wabi-sabi requires subtle taste. If you copy the Japanese without understanding, it comes out as a "poor room" instead of a "deep" one. Learn the difference between minimalism from principle and minimalism from laziness. The first is beautiful. The second is just scarcity.

current_p1_ru: Mid-century modern, морской, марокканский, винтаж. Ты любишь, когда комната отсылает к эпохам. Не одной — нескольким сразу. И из этого микса получается твой собственный стиль.
current_p1_en:
Mid-century modern, coastal, Moroccan, vintage. You love a room that refers to eras. Not one — several at once. From that mix, your own style appears.
You have an eye for design. Each era has its own rhythm, and you can combine the best of several in one space.
People sometimes ask: "is everything from a flea market?" Not from a flea market — from different eras, chosen on purpose. Different things.
What's worth knowing: a mix of eras works as long as there's a common thread. Without it it's just "a dump of good things". Learn to find this thread — maybe a common palette, or one country, or one material. Then your vintage mix turns into a style, not a collection.

I don't look for someone to blame
current_p1_ru: Слушаю по-настоящему, помню важные мелочи, умею молчать рядом, отвечаю честно «как ты». Твой green flag — внимание к другому. Не «киваю и думаю о своём»; а реально вовлечён(-а).
current_p1_en:
You really listen, remember the small things, can sit in silence with someone, and answer "how are you" honestly. Your green flag is attention to the other person. Not nodding while thinking your own thoughts — real involvement.
You have the rare ability to be present. Most people in conversation are already preparing what they'll say; you're thinking about the other person.
People love this in you: "you can be talked to." That may be the best compliment.
What's worth knowing: active listening exhausts. If you listen to everyone every day, there's no space for your own feelings. Take care of yourself. Sometimes you need to say: "right now I'm not in a state to listen." That's not selfish — it keeps the skill from breaking.

items_in_category: I can be silent next to you

I don't look for someone to blame
current_p1_ru: Говорю правду даже когда неудобно, держу слово, извиняюсь первым, могу сказать «я был неправ». Твой green flag — встроенная честность. Без оговорок.
current_p1_en:
You tell the truth even when it's uncomfortable, keep your word, apologize first, and can say "I was wrong." Your green flag is built-in honesty. No exceptions.
You have an inner spine. Most people bend the truth for convenience; you don't, and you're respected for it.
People sometimes say: "you're straight as an arrow." Straight, yes. And you sleep at night.
What's worth knowing: hard honesty sometimes wounds. Learn to tell "the truth needs to be said" from "the truth needs to be said this way". Form matters. The same truth, delivered gently, is still truth — but doesn't destroy.

items_in_category: I can be silent next to you
I don't gossip about loved ones
I don't look for someone to blame
current_p1_ru: Уважаю чужое «нет», не осуждаю за разные взгляды, не сплетничаю о близких, помогаю без ожидания. Твой green flag — настоящее уважение к границам.
current_p1_en:
You respect another person's "no," don't judge different views, don't gossip about loved ones, and help without expecting anything back. Your green flag is real respect for boundaries.
You have mature social ethics. Most people don't think much about boundaries; for you, they're baseline behavior.
People feel safe near you. And that's a rare feeling in the modern world.
What's worth knowing: respect for others' boundaries sometimes becomes ignoring your own. Learn to tell. Respect is mutual. Don't let others violate your boundaries just because you don't violate theirs.

items_in_category: I can be silent next to you
I don't gossip about loved ones
I don't look for someone to blame
current_p1_ru: Смеюсь над собой, радуюсь успехам друзей, не ищу виноватых, извиняюсь первым. Твой green flag — взрослые эмоции. Без драмы, без обиды, без зависти.
current_p1_en:
You laugh at yourself, celebrate friends' wins, don't look for someone to blame, and apologize first. Your green flag is adult emotion: no drama, no resentment, no envy.
You've worked through enough of your feelings to keep balance. Most people live on emotional swings; you don't let every swing become weather.
People are sometimes surprised by your calm: "how can you be happy she got the promotion, not you?" You can. Her joy isn't your loss.
What's worth knowing: emotional maturity requires constant work. Not "I have it, that's all"; daily practice. Don't let the muscle weaken. Without work, envy, resentment, and drama return — they're the default state.
